name: detect-boundary
note: Detector-triggered runs (answers 'the alert is an oracle'): no alert is injected; the monitor's own boundary detectors are the only alert source. One workload per detectable boundary fault on C2 and rand-n7-s1, each on the main grid's faulty invocation (L1.a, a4.s0.t1): out_of_scope_dispatch (it also hands its result to an agent outside its grant: agentd denies it, permission_denied, read by admission_denied) and, in the part, deadline_runaway (it hands on its work, then runs past the 1.5 x compute deadline its dispatcher set: agentd expires it, deadline_expired, read by lease_violation). Trace & quarantine, Firebreak and No containment, 3 repetitions, plus one no-fault reference per base workload and repetition (a false-alarm control; the part would repeat them): 2 x 3 x 4 + 2 x 3 x 3 = 42 runs. Profile, latency (native L = 400 ms), time scale, timeouts and root_wait_s as lab-main (root_wait_s has no effect: no alert is posted). The effect-level variants (c2-oos, c2-runaway, rand-n7-s1-oos, rand-n7-s1-runaway) stay in workloads/ but not in this grid: their violations are refused at the gateway and open no incident (H13c). Scored by the same scorer: alert_source 'detector', detected, detection_latency_ms, and the decision and tau_1 timings from the detector alert.
